codebase.title: MAS: Magnetohydrodynamic Algorithm outside a Sphere (the MHD engine of CORHEL and CORHEL-CME)
codebase.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA-256 over typed sorted regular-file paths+bytes and symlink paths+safe targets

agent_authored.description: MAS (Magnetohydrodynamic Algorithm outside a Sphere) is Predictive Science Inc.'s Fortran code that integrates the time-dependent resistive, viscous, thermodynamic MHD equations in 3D spherical coordinates from the solar surface to 1 AU and beyond: potential-field or dipole starts anchored in a photospheric magnetic map, anisotropic thermal conduction, radiative losses, coronal heating models, Alfven-wave pressure and wave-turbulence-driven heating, flux-rope insertion (RBSL and TDm) for CME modelling, heliospheric runs driven by boundary files, on CPUs with MPI and on NVIDIA GPUs. It is the MHD engine of CORHEL and CORHEL-CME at NASA's Community Coordinated Modeling Center; the entry point for this codebase was the CCMC CORHEL-CME model page, whose web framework is not published.
evidence: the CCMC CORHEL-CME model page (https:ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov, models, CORHEL-CME~1)

approval.human_ref: single-module default: the whole codebase is one module; no human decision at STOP 1, the cut is read in the source PR body at STOP 2

build.system: build.sh + generated make (conf file gives FC, FRTFLAGS, HDF5 include and lib paths; build.sh writes src/Makefile from Makefile.template, compiles the expmac macro expander, expands src/mas.F90 into src/mas_cpp.f90, compiles pchip_module_v1.0.0.f90 and mas_cpp.f90, links with -lhdf5_fortran -lhdf5_hl_fortran -lhdf5 -lhdf5_hl, and moves the executable to bin/mas)
commands: cp conf/gcc_cpu_mac_brew.conf conf/gcc_cpu_mac_brew_local.conf; edit HDF5_INCLUDE_DIR to the Homebrew prefix include directory and HDF5_LIB_DIR to the Homebrew prefix lib directory (arm64 Homebrew)
bash build.sh conf/gcc_cpu_mac_brew_local.conf   (FC mpif90 = gfortran 15.2 under Open MPI 5.0.8, FRTFLAGS -O3 -march=native, HDF5 1.14.6 serial with Fortran)
pitfalls: the shipped conf/gcc_cpu_mac_brew.conf points HDF5 at the Intel Homebrew prefix (Intel Homebrew); on Apple silicon Homebrew lives under the opt homebrew prefix, so the two HDF5 paths must be edited, otherwise the link fails on hdf5.mod
the compile is one 74k-line translation unit at -O3 (63 s of the 68 s); there is no parallel make

HDF5 must be built with the same Fortran compiler as FC (the Fortran .mod files are compiler-specific); Homebrew hdf5 (serial) with mpif90 wrapping the same gfortran links fine, no parallel HDF5 is required

landscape.how_to_run: cd testsuite && bash run_test_suite.sh [-np=N] [-test=<name>] [-nocleanup] (needs bin/ on PATH or it appends it; python3 with numpy and h5py); each test copies input/ into run/, runs `mpirun -np N mas <name> mas.in`, then bin/mas_compare_run_diags.py compares the last line of mas_history_a.out against reference/ to 6 decimal digits
landscape.notes: reference/ holds mas.log, mas.out, mas_history_a.out, mas_history_b.out, mas_run_parameters_used.out and mas_timing.out from PSI's run (GCC 12.3, x86 alderlake, 4 ranks in a 2x1x2 decomposition); no HDF5 fields are shipped as reference. Six older tests listed as comments in the script (poly_1d_parker, poly_2d_shear, poly_2d_dipole, poly_2d_ip_cs, thermo_1d_wind, wtd_1d_analytic) have no directories in the tree

landscape.how_to_run: in the deck directory, mpirun -np N the built mas executable <run_name> mas.in (the coronal decks read the sibling input_data directory  by relative path; the heliospheric decks read their own bc/ directory)
landscape.notes: production steady-state relaxations: corona_polytropic_cr2124 (201x151x257, tmax 150), corona_thermo_hm1_cr2124 and corona_thermo_hm2_cr2124 (255x143x300, tmax 120, HM1 and HM2 heating), corona_thermo_hm1_tilted_dipole (231x125x217, tmax 2.49), heliosphere_tmhdhm1_bc_cr2124 and heliosphere_wsa_bc_cr2124 (500x157x361, r0 30 Rs, tmax 600, boundary slices from a thermodynamic coronal run or from WSA)

pitfalls.symptom: link fails or hdf5.mod not found with the shipped mac conf on Apple silicon
pitfalls.workaround: edit the two HDF5 paths in the conf to the Homebrew prefix include directory and the Homebrew prefix lib directory

pitfalls.symptom: run_test_suite.sh -test=a,b reports "TEST a' is not a valid test" under macOS bash 3.2: the comma-to-space substitution inserts literal quotes
pitfalls.workaround: pass one test per -test= (or run under bash 5); the full suite with no -test works

pitfalls.symptom: the reference comparison compares the first 6 significant digits of each history value as strings but copies the exponent from the reference file (num1[-4:]) for both, so a difference only in the exponent is not caught; and the -compareprec default is 6 while the help text says 5
pitfalls.workaround: for the checks, grade the history columns numerically (relative tolerance), not with mas_compare_run_diags.py

pitfalls.symptom: the speed-up line calls `python`, not python3; on a host without a python alias it prints a traceback after the run (the PASS/FAIL verdict is unaffected)
pitfalls.workaround: provide a python shim or ignore the line

pitfalls.symptom: the final history values depend on the MPI rank count at the 1e-8 relative level (semi-implicit PCG solves)
pitfalls.workaround: fix the rank count in every check; calibrate the tolerance for that rank count

pitfalls.symptom: mpirun (Open MPI 5 prterun) ignores SIGALRM, so `perl -e 'alarm N; exec @ARGV'` does not stop a run; the six-minute production-grid runs had to be killed by hand
pitfalls.workaround: launch under a wrapper that kills the whole process group (start_new_session + killpg), as the runto.py wrapper did

pitfalls.symptom: production decks take minutes per step on 4 ranks (7.8M to 28M cells with 1e-9 CG tolerances)
pitfalls.workaround: reduce nr, nt, np and set ntmax for smoke runs; a check at this size needs its own reduced grid and window, recorded as a knob

modules.title: MAS: thermodynamic resistive MHD of the solar corona and inner heliosphere in 3D spherical coordinates
entrypoints: the mas executable built from src/mas.F90 (mpirun -np N mas RUN_NAME mas.in); testsuite/run_test_suite.sh; the examples decks mas.in
modules.expensive_path: the per-step MHD advance on the 3D spherical staggered grid: the semi-implicit velocity and viscosity solves (advv, v_solver: preconditioned conjugate gradient, 60 percent of the thermo_3d_relaxation step time), the field-aligned thermal conduction solve (advtce), the vector-potential advance (adva), and the potential-field initialisation (pot_3d) on production grids of 8 to 28 million cells; upstream's own GPU port (OpenACC and do concurrent under nvfortran) is the record to beat
modules.rationale: One code, one build, one executable, one namelist, one test suite: every physics switch (zero-beta, polytropic, thermodynamic with conduction, radiation and heating models, pressure waves, WTD turbulence, charge states, tracer particles, heliospheric boundary files) is a namelist option of the same 73k-line program and shares the grid, the MPI decomposition, the CG solvers and the HDF5 I/O. The whole codebase is one module.
hazards: final energies depend on the MPI rank count at the 1e-8 relative level in the thermodynamic decks (semi-implicit PCG reductions); the zero-beta and 2D heliospheric decks were rank-independent to 12 digits
the shipped references were made on x86 (GCC 12.3, alderlake, 4 ranks); the suite's own bar is 6 decimal digits, met here on arm64 with gfortran 15
single-file source pre-processed by PSI's expmac macro expander; a port has to keep the build (build.sh, conf file) working
needs HDF5 with Fortran bindings built by the same compiler, and an MPI library; no other external dependency
the upstream README asks research users to contact support@predsci.com (Apache-2.0 licence otherwise)
the production example decks cost minutes per step; checks derived from them need a reduced grid and a short window
modules.purpose: The whole code is one module: one executable (bin/mas from src/mas.F90), one namelist, one test suite; every physics regime is a switch of the same program sharing the grid, the MPI decomposition, the conjugate-gradient solvers and the HDF5 I/O.
primary_inputs: mas.in namelist (topology and data groups: grid, domain, time, physics switches, solver tolerances, output lists)

a photospheric radial-field map (HDF5, theta-phi) or a dipole, 1D or 2D initial plasma profiles, optional flux-rope path files, WTD masks and limits, and for heliospheric runs a bc directory of boundary slices
primary_outputs: mas_history_a.out and mas_history_b.out (energies, CFL, conservation diagnostics per step), in-situ histories
3D fields and tp slices in HDF5 (rho, t, p, v, b, j, heat, em, ep, potfld_*), restart files, mas.log, mas_timing.out
algorithm_stages: mesh generation and MPI decomposition in r, theta, phi
potential-field initialisation (pot_2d, pot_3d: conjugate gradient) or analytic field, flux-rope insertion (RBSL, TDm)

per step: density advance, semi-implicit temperature and field-aligned conduction solves (advte, advtce), vector-potential advance (adva), semi-implicit velocity and viscosity solves (advv, v_solver, PCG), wave models (advpw, advzw), particles
unique_responsibilities: the coronal and heliospheric MHD solution
not_responsible_for: magnetogram preparation (MagMAP, psi-io), WSA boundary generation (SWiG), field-line tracing (MapFL), visualisation (PsiPy, pyvisual), the CORHEL-CME web workflow
evidence: src/mas.F90 (73,592 lines, 118 Fortran modules), testsuite (8 decks with references), examples (6 production decks)
runs.json: native build 68 s, all 8 tests reproduced to 6 digits, 3 examples run at reduced size
modules.classification: agent-authored module card; CLI-computed size and approval status
